open_points.subject: Authored TrialCase port set
open_points.text: `functions.add_trial_case` takes "input values by port, optional expected outputs" and enforces "Fit in port name order — presence, carriage, schema, size", but does not say whether extra port names are refused or whether present `expected_outputs` must contain every output port.
open_points.question: Must authored trial inputs name exactly every input port and no others, and must expected outputs be either wholly absent or name exactly every output port and no others?
options: Require exact input keys and, when expected outputs are present, exact output keys
Ignore extra keys while requiring declared ports
Allow partial expected outputs and compare only those supplied
open_points.default_guess: Require exact input keys and make expected outputs either absent or exact.

open_points.subject: Many-file references and disclosure class
open_points.text: M23 says inputs and outputs contain references "to SpooledFiles by their facts, by port", while A13 says a file-list reference "carries the list's class" and an empty list retains the highest class among the node's inputs; M22 stores only each individual file's class, and State 5 passes operation inputs as "StoredValues and SpooledFiles".
open_points.question: Where is the disclosure class of a `many` file value represented, especially for an empty list or a list whose elements have different classes?
options: Add a list-reference wrapper containing ordered SpooledFile identities and the list class
Store the list class separately in each NodeExecution port reference
Derive it from element records, with a separately recorded class for an empty list
open_points.default_guess: Use a port-level ordered file-list reference carrying the list class.

open_points.subject: Operation failure detail recording
open_points.text: M23 provides only one `failure_detail` field, but `service_invoker.send_prepared_request` returns both an `operation_failed` detail code such as `redirect_not_followed` and "a bounded `failure_detail`" derived from the response body; State 5 separately declares a closed set of machine-relevant detail codes.
open_points.question: How must both the closed detail code and the diagnostic response-body text be represented in the resulting NodeExecution and returned trace?
options: Add a separate `detail_code` field to NodeExecution
Store only the closed code and discard diagnostic body text
Store only diagnostic text and lose the closed code
Combine both into one prescribed string
open_points.default_guess: Add a separate optional `detail_code` and retain bounded `failure_detail` independently.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution timestamps without execution or send
open_points.text: The State 5 convention says `started_at` is taken "when the execution or send begins", but NodeExecutions are also written for `skipped_by_guard`, `upstream_failed`, mapped nodes over empty lists, pre-send `operation_failed`, and `refused_by_owner`, where no execution or send begins.
open_points.question: What values must `started_at` and `ended_at` have for each NodeExecution that represents no execution or send?
options: Set both to the time the conclusion is recorded
Set `started_at` when the node first becomes ready and `ended_at` when concluded
Make `started_at` absent for non-executed records
open_points.default_guess: Set both timestamps to the store-change time that records the conclusion.

open_points.subject: Inputs recorded for non-executed NodeExecutions
open_points.text: M23 requires `inputs` and `outputs` by port, and A13 explicitly says a receiving node rejected before running names "the inputs it had", but no rule says what inputs are recorded for `skipped_by_guard`, `upstream_failed`, or a mapped node over an empty list.
open_points.question: Which input references must those non-executed NodeExecutions contain: all values already available, only the decisive input, the complete logical input including missing-port markers, or none?
options: Record every input value available at conclusion and omit unavailable ports
Record no inputs for any non-executed node
Record a complete port map with explicit unavailable reasons
open_points.default_guess: Record every available input reference and omit ports that never received a value.

open_points.subject: Recording an unconfirmed sandbox cleanup
open_points.text: State 3 and State 4 say that after unconfirmed cleanup `runs` writes the NodeExecution but "writes no run status"; State 5 says the only runs-owned change that writes NodeExecutions, `record_run_progress`, writes the NodeExecutions "then the run's status, outputs, WaitingPoints M20, `ended_at`, `cancelled_by`".
open_points.question: Which store change writes the cleanup-failure NodeExecution while deliberately leaving the run status untouched?
options: Allow `record_run_progress` to write NodeExecutions without a Run update in this case
Add a dedicated change for the cleanup-failure NodeExecution
Write the Run again with its unchanged `running` status
open_points.default_guess: Permit a cleanup-failure form of `record_run_progress` that writes only the NodeExecution and leaves the Run record unchanged.

open_points.subject: Repair-view continuation token
open_points.text: `get_repair_view` says its continuation token "also carries the implementation set of its first page", while a slot may have an unbounded number of implementations and A16 bounds every request string by `bounded_text_bytes_max`.
open_points.question: How can the continuation token preserve an arbitrarily large frozen implementation set while remaining within the request-field bound?
options: Represent the frozen set by a first-page store-position cutoff and reconstruct it
Persist server-side paging state and put only its bounded identity in the token
Impose a previously unstated maximum on implementations per slot
Allow the token to exceed `bounded_text_bytes_max`
open_points.default_guess: Carry a bounded store-position cutoff from which the frozen implementation set can be reconstructed.

open_points.subject: Store privacy check
open_points.text: `store.open_store` enforces a "private directory" and State 2 says "The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user", but neither text fixes the ownership and permission test for the directory and pre-existing database, value, fixture, spool, and lock files.
open_points.question: Exactly which owner, mode, and recursive-entry conditions must `open_store` accept or refuse?
options: Require the kernel user to own the directory and every entry, with no group or other permissions
Check only the root directory for kernel-user ownership and no group or other permissions
Require exact modes such as 0700 for directories and 0600 for files
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership and no group or other permission bits on the root and every existing entry.
